---
title: "Engineering log"
---

Design decisions, refactors, numerical stability issues, data layout and
performance choices. It supplements the git history with the reasoning.
Entries are dated H2 sections; existing entries are never edited.

## 2026-11-05: Step 0, project scaffolding

**Double precision.** `jax_enable_x64` is set in `jaxdft/_config.py`, the
first import in `jaxdft/__init__.py`. Any entry point that imports anything
from the package therefore enables x64 before any array exists. The test suite
checks this in a fresh subprocess as well as in-process, because
`tests/conftest.py` imports `jaxdft` for every test and would otherwise hide a
broken import order.

`jaxdft.precision.assert_double_precision` walks a pytree and rejects any
inexact leaf that is not float64 or complex128. Integer and boolean leaves
(Miller indices, masks) are ignored. Physics tests should call it on their
outputs. This is how "a test must fail if any physical array is float32" is
enforced in practice.

**Test configuration.**

- `--import-mode=importlib`, so the three test directories can contain
  files with the same name without `__init__.py` packages.
- `filterwarnings = error`: a warning from JAX (e.g. an implicit dtype
  truncation) fails the test rather than scrolling past.
- `--strict-markers`, with one marker, `slow`, defined up front.
- Hypothesis runs with `deadline=None`, because the first call of a jitted
  function includes tracing and compilation, so per-example timing is
  meaningless. Two profiles: `default` (50 examples, for laptops) and `ci`
  (200), selected with `HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE`.

**Dependencies.** `pytest` and `hypothesis` are in the `dev` group, `altair`
and `jupyter` in `docs`. Both are uv default groups, since the definition of
done needs both, so a plain `uv sync` installs everything.

**Docs execution.** `execute.freeze` is explicitly `false`. Documents compute
their numbers from `jaxdft` at render time, and freezing would let a document
go stale against the code without failing.

Quarto must find the project's virtual environment. It does when the venv is
active (it then picks `.venv/bin/python3` from `PATH`). From a plain shell it
falls back to the system Python and fails. I tried a `docs/_environment` file
setting `QUARTO_PYTHON`. Quarto resolves that relative path against the
directory it is invoked from, not the project, so it broke depending on where
the command was run, and I removed it. `uv run quarto render docs/` works from
any shell and is the robust form of the definition-of-done command.

**Removed.** The `jaxdft` console-script entry point and its `main()`
placeholder from the `uv init` template. A command-line interface will be
added when there is something to run.

**Deferred.**

- The shared plot-style module arrives with the first plot (Milestone 1a
  validation). It will live outside the physics so that `altair` stays a docs
  dependency.
- A `units` module with tested conversions arrives with the first
  boundary conversion. Milestone 1a works entirely in atomic units and in
  units of $\tfrac12(2\pi/a)^2$.
